pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: You declare `--format` with `root.PersistentFlags()` and `--tag` with `addCmd.Flags()`. Which commands can read each one, and how would you check that in code?
expected_points: a persistent flag is visible on the command that declared it and every descendant, at any depth
a local flag exists only on the command that declared it — `list` cannot see `add`'s `--tag`
cmd.Flags() is local plus inherited; LocalFlags() is what this command declared; InheritedFlags() is what came from ancestors
a persistent flag can be typed before or after the subcommand name

questions.prompt: Why does a cobra handler use `RunE` and return an error instead of calling `os.Exit(1)` when something goes wrong?
expected_points: os.Exit ends the process immediately: defers do not run and buffers do not flush
a test cannot call that path in-process — it would kill the test binary
the error travels back out of Execute so exactly one place, main, maps it to an exit code
log.Fatal and cobra.CheckErr have the same problem

questions.prompt: What do `SilenceErrors` and `SilenceUsage` change, and what do they deliberately not change?
expected_points: SilenceErrors stops cobra printing `Error: ...` to stderr itself
SilenceUsage stops it dumping the usage block after a runtime failure
Execute still returns the error either way — they change who prints, not what happens
with both set, main is the single reporter, so tests can assert stderr is empty

questions.prompt: Walk me through how your test runs `notes add "x" --format json` without starting a process. Which calls are involved, and why is the tree rebuilt for every test?
expected_points: build the tree with a constructor, SetOut/SetErr to buffers, SetArgs, then Execute
handlers write to cmd.OutOrStdout() so the buffer captures everything
a cobra.Command stores parsed flag values on itself, so a shared tree leaks state between runs
dependencies arrive through an App struct rather than globals, so the test supplies its own store and env lookup

questions.prompt: Your resolver layers default < environment < flag into one Settings struct. What role does the flag's `Changed` field play, and what breaks without it?
expected_points: Changed reports whether the user actually typed the flag, as opposed to it sitting at its default
without it the default value overwrites whatever the environment supplied
Lookup returning nil tells you the command cannot see that flag at all
everything lands in one struct so handlers never re-derive configuration

questions.prompt: A colleague is starting a tool with one command and four flags and asks whether to use cobra. What do you tell them, and what would change your answer?
expected_points: stdlib flag is enough for a single command: no dependency, tiny API
cobra earns its keep with a command tree, generated help, completions and suggestions
it costs three modules and a large API surface
flag syntax differs (-flag vs POSIX --flag/-f), so switching later changes the tool's published interface

questions.prompt: Viper is cobra's usual companion. What does it buy you, and what does it cost?
expected_points: buys: config files in several formats, automatic env binding, BindPFlag, Unmarshal into a struct
costs: the package-level API is a process-wide singleton, so tests share state — use viper.New()
costs: case-insensitive nested key resolution makes 'where did this value come from?' hard to answer
reasonable when there are many sources and keys; below that a readable hand-rolled resolver wins

questions.prompt: `notes tag` exists only to hold `tag add` and `tag list`. If you give it no RunE, what happens when a user types `notes tag bogus`, and why?
expected_points: cobra decides a non-runnable command needs help before it validates arguments
so it prints help and returns no error — exit code 0 on a typo, which scripts cannot detect
fix: give the group a RunE that calls cmd.Help() plus Args: cobra.NoArgs
then the typo becomes `unknown command "bogus" for "notes tag"`
